theory.intro: Many real-life problems combine fractional amounts or find how much remains. When the denominators match, add or subtract the numerators only.
facts: Fractions of the same whole with the same denominator have **same-size parts**.
Keep the **denominator the same** — only the numerators change.
Read what is known and what is asked. Add to combine amounts; subtract to find how much remains.
steps: Read what is known and what is asked. Decide whether to combine amounts or find how much remains.
Add or subtract the numerators and keep the common denominator.
Simplify the answer if possible and include the units when needed.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two ribbons measure $\frac{2}{9}$ m and $\frac{4}{9}$ m.
(a) Find their total length.
(b) A third ribbon measures $\frac{1}{9}$ m. Find the total length of all three ribbons.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{2}{9}+\frac{4}{9}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$ m
(b) $\frac{2}{9}+\frac{4}{9}+\frac{1}{9}=\frac{7}{9}$ m
Add the numbers of ninths and keep the denominator $9$.

workedExamples.question_text: A jug contains $\frac{13}{15}$ L. After $\frac{7}{15}$ L is poured out, how much is left?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract the amount poured out.
$\frac{13}{15}-\frac{7}{15}=\frac{6}{15}=\frac{2}{5}$ L

workedExamples.question_text: Separate parts of a board are painted: red paint covers $\frac{11}{16}$ of the board and blue paint covers $\frac{5}{16}$. What fraction of the board is painted?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the painted amounts.
$\frac{11}{16}+\frac{5}{16}=\frac{16}{16}=1$
The whole board is painted.

workedExamples.question_text: Mia reads $\frac{10}{19}$ of a novel on Monday and a further $\frac{3}{19}$ on Tuesday. What fraction is still unread?
workedExamples.solution_text:
First find the fraction read.
$\frac{10}{19}+\frac{3}{19}=\frac{13}{19}$
The whole novel is $\frac{19}{19}$.
$\frac{19}{19}-\frac{13}{19}=\frac{6}{19}$
The unread fraction is $\frac{6}{19}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Two ribbons measure $\frac{17}{22}$ m and $\frac{8}{22}$ m. What is their total length?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\frac{17}{22}+\frac{8}{22}=\frac{25}{22}$ m
The total length is $\frac{25}{22}$ m.

workedExamples.question_text: A walker has completed $\frac{18}{28}$ of a route. What fraction of the route is left?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract the fraction completed from the whole route.
$1-\frac{18}{28}=\frac{28}{28}-\frac{18}{28}=\frac{10}{28}=\frac{5}{14}$
The fraction left is $\frac{5}{14}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Three friends eat $\frac{1}{10}$, $\frac{3}{10}$ and $\frac{2}{10}$ of the same pizza. What fraction of the pizza is left?
A piece of ribbon needs to be $\frac{11}{8}$ m long. Hana has $\frac{7}{8}$ m. How much more ribbon does she need?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract the length she has from the length needed.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{11}{8}-\frac{7}{8}\\&=\frac{4}{8}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$
She needs $\frac{1}{2}$ m more ribbon.
